question: Let P=((1)/(x)-(1)/(y))[(x+y)²-xy]+((1)/(x)+(1)/(y))[(x-y)²+xy] and Q = (y)/(x), then P ÷ Q is equal to:
solution:
**Given:**

** P=((1)/(x)-(1)/(y))[(x+y)²-xy]+((1)/(x)+(1)/(y))[(x-y)²+xy]**

Q = (y)/(x)

**Concept Used:**

(a³ - b³) = (a - b)(a² + b² + ab)

(a3 + b3) = (a + b)(a2 + b² - ab)

**Calculation:**

 P=((1)/(x)-(1)/(y))[(x+y)²-xy]+((1)/(x)+(1)/(y))[(x-y)²+xy]

⇒ P=((1)/(x)-(1)/(y))[x²+y²+2xy-xy]+((1)/(x)+(1)/(y))[x²+y²-2xy+xy]

⇒ P=((y-x)/(xy))[x²+y²+xy]+((x+y)/(xy))[x²+y²-xy]

⇒ P=((y³-x³)/(xy))+((x³+y³)/(xy))

⇒ P=((y³-x³+x³+y³)/(xy))

⇒ P=((2y³)/(xy))

⇒ P=((2y²)/(x))

P ÷ Q = ((2y²)/(x)) div (y)/(x)

⇒ ((2y²)/(x)) times (x)/(y)

⇒ 2y

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**
